headnotes.en: …amely for the freedom of its nature from death and diabolical servitude, and from ignorance of the truth, but the intellectual for knowing its cause, of which before it was ignorant. Hence the Apostle

headnotes.en: …hout reason asked why in the Old Testament and in the New it is frequently read of God that he appeared to men, whether visibly to carnal eyes, or invisibly in prophetic visions, while the Gospel says

headnotes.la: …ritus sancti saepe intelligantur visibiliter apparuisse, solum vero Patrem remotum ab omni visione. Quoniam vero non de una persona, sed de sola Trinitate, quae Deus unus est, hoc intelligitur dictum,
headnotes.en: …be understood often to have appeared visibly, but the Father alone to be removed from all vision. But since this is understood to be said not of one person, but of the Trinity alone, which is one God,

headnotes.en: … divine contemplation. To this it must be said that no partaker of human or angelic nature can contemplate God himself through himself in his own proper nature. For what is written in the Latin codex,

headnotes.en: …see God, if they do not see God himself, whom they are reported to see? For example, to set down a few examples out of many, Isaias saw the Lord sitting upon a high throne. The Lord says in the Gospel

headnotes.en: … souls and intellects there are theophanies, and in them, as they seek and love him, God manifests himself, in which, as in certain clouds, the saints are caught up to meet Christ, as the Apostle says

headnotes.en: , calling clouds the most bright heights of divine *theoria*, in which they will be always with Christ. Hence it is that Dionysius says

headnotes.la: …tum sanctum suum hominibus manifestaret et angelis, accepit. Nam humana anima, dum per se ipsam invisibilis sit, per motus suos corporeos, non quid sit, sed quia sit, manifestat. Et quid est, quod ait
headnotes.en: …d also his Holy Spirit, to men and to angels. For the human soul, while it is invisible through itself, manifests through its bodily motions not what it is, but that it is. And what is it that he says

headnotes.en: or

headnotes.la: …us Filius ipse est sinus Patris. Sinus autem Patris dicitur Filius, quia Patrem insinuavit mundo. Sinus etiam Patris unigenitus Filius est, quia in secretis paternae naturae semper est, sicut ipse ait
headnotes.en: …because he intimated (*insinuavit*) the Father to the world. The only-begotten Son is also the bosom of the Father, because he is always in the secret places of the paternal nature, as he himself says

headnotes.la: . Quemadmodum igitur domus Patris unigenitus Filius est, sicut ipse ait
headnotes.en: . Just as, therefore, the only-begotten Son is the house of the Father, as he himself says

headnotes.la: …tione [vl: 1 | cod. *doctrinam et manifestationem*.] suae incarnationis Deum invisibilem demonstravit et demonstrat et demonstraturus est; sicut ait in ipsa sententia, quam paulo superius introduximus
headnotes.en: …ed;* that is, by the teaching and manifestation of his incarnation he has shown the invisible God, and shows him, and will show him; as he says in that very sentence which we introduced a little above

headnotes.la: *Et hoc est testimonium Joannis.* Ac si diceret: Hoc totum, quod diximus, ab eo loco
headnotes.en: *And this is the testimony of John.* As if he said: All this which we have said, from that place

headnotes.la: usque ad id quod est,
headnotes.en: as far as that which is

headnotes.en: …ost severe terror of the vengeance to come. And besides this they thought that he, John I mean, was some one of the prophets risen again, seeing that the greatest grace of prophecy had advanced in him

headnotes.la: *Ego sum vox clamantis in deserto.* Si quaeritis, inquit, quid de me ipso profero, cognoscite, quia ego sum vox. Non dixit,
headnotes.en: *I am the voice of one crying in the desert.* If you ask, he says, what I put forth concerning myself, know that I am the voice. He did not say,

headnotes.en: , but he said

headnotes.la: … omnium, Dei Filius est. Ipse est enim, ut ait sanctus Augustinus, intellectus omnium, imo omnia. Cujus praecursor pulchre vocis vocabulo nominatur, quia primo per ipsum demonstratus est mundo, dicens
headnotes.en: …s, as saint Augustine says, the intellect of all things, nay rather all things. His forerunner is beautifully named by the word voice, because through him he was first shown to the world, when he said

headnotes.la: … quippe interpretatur remotio et excelsitudo, quod omnino divinae convenit naturae. In ipso itaque deserto divinae celsitudinis Verbum clamat, per quod facta sunt omnia. Audi Moysen in Genesi dicentem
headnotes.en: …moval and loftiness, which altogether befits the divine nature. In this very desert of the divine loftiness, therefore, the Word cries, through which all things were made. Hear Moses saying in Genesis

headnotes.en: . Where by the name of God we understand the Father, but

headnotes.en: …is divinity alone before the incarnation; he cried afterwards through his flesh. And what does that voice of his, that is, his forerunner, cry aloud? Hear. *Make straight the way of the Lord.* What is

headnotes.la: ? Nonne quod sequitur,
headnotes.en: ? Is it not what follows,

headnotes.la: ? Dirigite ergo viam Domini, hoc est, recte praedicate et credite Dominum, qui via est, sicut ipse ait
headnotes.en: ? Make straight therefore the way of the Lord, that is, rightly preach and believe the Lord, who is the way, as he himself says

headnotes.la: . Potest et sic intelligi

headnotes.en: …d: The Pharisees especially, for this reason, hearing that the preaching of John had persuaded the people of the general resurrection of all from the dead, and most of all in that place where he says,

headnotes.la: …ssisse, eumque Heliam et Elisaeum siccis pedibus transiisse, figuram baptismatis in Helia et Elisaeo non dubitabant praecessisse, aut illos ipsos surrexisse ac baptizasse. Ac per hoc non interrogabant
headnotes.en: …d Eliseus crossed it with dry feet, they did not doubt that the figure of baptism had gone before in Elias and Eliseus, or that those very men had risen and baptized. And through this they did not ask

headnotes.en: ? but only

headnotes.la: …am calceamenti ejus subtilitatem, et investigabilem perplexionem mysteriorum incarnationis intellige. Cujus mysterii altitudinem solvere indignum se praecursor judicat. Notandum tamen, quod non dixit,
headnotes.en: … subtlety and unsearchable perplexity of the mysteries of the incarnation. The height of which mystery the forerunner judges himself unworthy to loose. It is to be noted, however, that he did not say,

headnotes.la: , sed dixit
headnotes.en: , but he said

headnotes.la: …jus densissimas caligines, et a luce veritatis valde remotas. Secundum sacerdotium est in Novo Testamento; quod a praedicatione praecursoris incipit, et in fine mundi terminabitur, sicut ait Scriptura
headnotes.en: … and very remote from the light of truth. The second priesthood is in the New Testament; which begins from the preaching of the forerunner, and will be ended at the end of the world, as Scripture says

headnotes.la: … caste, omnique carnalis conversationis contagione remota, veluti in quadam solitudine divinarum virtutum debent vivere, ut Joannes. Legem quoque scriptam Joannes significat, quoniam ipsius finis est;
headnotes.en: … and chastely, with all contagion of carnal conversation removed, ought to live as it were in a certain solitude of divine virtues, like John. John also signifies the written law, since he is its end;

headnotes.la: . Quoniam vero non solum propheta, verum etiam manifestator Christi factus est, non modo legem significat solam, sed et Evangelium et gratiam. Ideoque sequitur
headnotes.en: . But since he was made not only a prophet, but also the manifester of Christ, he signifies not only the law alone, but also the Gospel and grace. And therefore there follows

headnotes.la: …icantius scribitur, *alia die videt Joannes Jesum venientem ad se.* Alia, inquit, die, hoc est, alia cognitione. Prima enim cognitio fuit, quando eum concurrentibus ibidem populis manifestavit, dicens
headnotes.en: … seeth Jesus coming to him.* On another day, he says, that is, by another knowledge. For the first knowledge was when he made him manifest to the peoples who had flocked together in that place, saying

headnotes.la: …esus ad Joannem, hoc est, dignatus est cognosci ab Joanne secundum divinitatem suam et humanitatem. Et ait: *Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccatum mundi.* Manifeste eum populis praedicat, dum dicit
headnotes.en: …d to be known by John according to his divinity and humanity. And he says: *Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world.* He openly preaches him to the peoples when he says

headnotes.la: …n enim primus Adam ille, qui ex generalitate naturae humanae ante ceteros in mundum hunc visibilem venit, solus peccavit, sed omnes peccaverunt, priusquam in mundum procederent. Nam quod Apostolus ait
headnotes.en: …t that first Adam alone, who out of the generality of human nature came into this visible world before the rest, sinned, but all sinned before they went forth into the world. For what the Apostle says

headnotes.la: …taque originale peccatum, singulorumque post generationem in hunc mundum delicta, gratiae baptismatis abundantia per Salvatorem nostrum relaxantur, ut omnino non sint. Et hoc est, quod ait evangelista
headnotes.en: …es of individuals after their generation into this world, are loosed by the abundance of the grace of baptism through our Saviour, so that they altogether are not. And this is what the evangelist says

headnotes.la: …, et intellectualiter mente, non dente, comedimus [fn: b | En ineptiarum, quas, teste Adrevaldo, J. Scotus de SS. Eucharistia docuit, vestigia. E contra Berengarius Romanae subscribere debuit formulae
headnotes.en: … not with the tooth [nt: Here are traces of the absurdities which, as Adrevald witnesses, J. Scotus taught concerning the Holy Eucharist. Against them Berengarius had to subscribe to the Roman formula

headnotes.la: …ionem effectus, hoc est, praecedet interemptio originalis peccati in omnibus et in singulis interemptionem mortis; similiter in toto et in parte, quando etiam implebitur, quod dictum est per prophetam
headnotes.en: …at is, the slaying of original sin in all and in individuals will go before the slaying of death; likewise in the whole and in the part, when that also shall be fulfilled which was said by the prophet

headnotes.la: …tes carnalium suarum cogitationum et actionum, veluti infidelium Judaeorum impetum atque invidiam, sola fide colloquio Christi fruuntur, bonorum operum fiduciam non habentes. Propterea Evangelista ait
headnotes.en: … assault and envy of their carnal thoughts and actions, as of the faithless Jews, they enjoy converse with Christ by faith alone, not having the confidence of good works. Therefore the Evangelist says

headnotes.la: …rit Deus cum eo.* Ex his verbis, quibus Nicodemus visus est Christum alloqui, datur intelligi, ipsum, Nicodemum dico, unum fuisse ex his, qui crediderunt paulo ante in die Pascha, de quibus dictum est
headnotes.en: …Nicodemus is seen to have addressed Christ, it is given to understand that he himself, Nicodemus I mean, was one of those who had believed a little before, on the day of the Pasch, of whom it was said

headnotes.en: …ν , that is, from above, so that we say "from above" for "anew"; which is both more easily understood, and more fitting to the two nativities, namely the earthly and the heavenly. For the Apostle says

headnotes.en: …ur Lord Jesus Christ also deigned to undergo for the salvation of human nature. Of which the first is that nativity in which the whole human race was born together from nothing; of which it is written

headnotes.la: . Secunda, quae hominis delictum subsecuta ex utroque sexu, ad similitudinem ceterorum animalium, de qua eadem Scriptura dicit
headnotes.en: . The second, which, following upon the offence of man, is from both sexes, after the likeness of the other animals, of which the same Scripture says

headnotes.la: ; per quam totum genus humanum in infinitum multiplicatur terrena successione. Tertia, quae est secundum spiritum, de qua nunc Dominus ait
headnotes.en: ; through which the whole human race is multiplied without limit by earthly succession. The third, which is according to the spirit, of which the Lord now says

headnotes.la: …d autem natura confert resurrectioni, et quid gratia, alius disserendi locus est. *Non potest videre regnum Dei.* Regni Dei multiplex intellectus est. Regnum Dei est ecclesia fidelium, de qua scriptum
headnotes.en: …race, is another place for discussion. *He cannot see the kingdom of God.* Of the kingdom of God the understanding is manifold. The kingdom of God is the church of the faithful, of which it is written

headnotes.la: . Regnum Dei universitas corporalis et spiritualis creaturae. Regnum Dei caelestes virtutes et justorum animae. Regnum Dei est Filius Dei, qui
headnotes.en: . The kingdom of God is the universe of corporeal and spiritual creation. The kingdom of God is the heavenly powers and the souls of the just. The kingdom of God is the Son of God, who

headnotes.la: …ptibile, et cetera, quae ad gloriam futurae resurrectionis pertinebunt. Verumtamen etiam in praesenti vita sanctificat fidelium corpora virtus sacramenti, cum templum Dei efficiantur, dicente Apostolo
headnotes.en: …he glory of the future resurrection. Nevertheless, even in the present life the power of the sacrament sanctifies the bodies of the faithful, since they are made the temple of God, as the Apostle says

headnotes.la: …t, hoc est, carnale est. Notandum, quod in hoc loco nomine carnis non carnem solummodo, sed totum carnalem hominem significaverit. Siquidem saepe anima carnalis carnis nomine vocitatur, unde Apostolus
headnotes.en: …arnal. It is to be noted that in this place by the name of flesh he signified not the flesh only, but the whole carnal man. For often the carnal soul is called by the name of flesh, whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: …ubi vult spirat, hoc est, operatur in his, in quibus vult operari, dividens singulis propria, prout vult. *Et vocem ejus audis.* De voce sancti Spiritus sat est verba sancti Augustini ponere. Ait enim
headnotes.en: … whom he wills to work, dividing to each their own, as he will. *And thou hearest his voice.* Concerning the voice of the Holy Spirit it is enough to set down the words of saint Augustine. For he says

headnotes.la: …m, unde venit et quo vadit? Noli hoc existimare. Nam si nascaris ex spiritu, non solum vocem ejus audies, verum etiam cognosces, unde venit et quo vadit. Venit a Patre per Filium, sicut alibi scriptum
headnotes.en: …uppose this. For if thou art born of the spirit, thou wilt not only hear its voice, but also know whence it comes and whither it goes. It comes from the Father through the Son, as is written elsewhere

headnotes.la: *Respondit Nicodemus et dixit ei: Quomodo possunt haec fieri?* Adhuc haesitat, qui litteram legis legerat, spiritum autem ipsius omnino ignorabat. Quod ait Apostolus
headnotes.en: *Nicodemus answered and said to him: How can these things be done?* He still hesitates, who had read the letter of the law but was altogether ignorant of its spirit. Which is what the Apostle says

headnotes.la: … est, quoniam ipse est veritas. Omne autem, quod ex veritate procedit, verum esse necesse est. Necnon et ipse Dominus locutio est Patris, et sermo Patris, et verbum ejus. De illo sermone Propheta ait,
headnotes.en: …himself is the truth. And all that proceeds from the truth must be true. Moreover the Lord himself is the speech of the Father, and the word of the Father, and his Word. Of that word the Prophet says,

headnotes.la: , et ipse de se ipso ait
headnotes.en: , and he himself says of himself

headnotes.la: …ativitatem ex spiritu docens, dixerit: *si terrena dicebam vobis?* Ad hoc dicendum, quia non ad praedicta respicit responsio, sed ad ea, quae superius in die Pascha dixerat quaerentibus signum Judaeis
headnotes.en: …elling earthly things to you?* To this it must be said that the answer looks back not to the foregoing, but to those things which he had said above, on the day of the Pasch, to the Jews seeking a sign

headnotes.la: …lo,* pulchre aliis verbis exponitur: nemo ascendit in Patrem, nisi qui de Patre descendit, filius hominis, qui est in Patre. Qualis autem descensus ejus et ascensus, ipse alibi aperte exposuit, dicens
headnotes.en: …an hath ascended into the Father, but he who descended from the Father, the son of man, who is in the Father. But of what kind his descent and ascent are, he himself expounded openly elsewhere, saying

headnotes.la: …est his, pro quibus descendit? Magna quidem et inexplicabilis, quoniam omnes, quos salvavit, in ipso ascendunt, nunc per fidem in spe, in fine vero per speciem in re, sicut ait Joannes in Epistola sua
headnotes.en: …e for those for whom he descended? Great indeed and inexplicable, since all whom he saved ascend in him, now through faith in hope, but at the end through sight in reality, as John says in his Epistle

headnotes.la: … in illo formetur, et unum cum Christo sit. Similiter nemo salvatur per mortem Christi, nisi qui ex spiritu nascitur; nemo ex spiritu nascitur per baptismum, nisi in morte Christi, sicut ait Apostolus
headnotes.en: … be one with Christ. Likewise no one is saved through the death of Christ but he who is born of the spirit; no one is born of the spirit through baptism but in the death of Christ, as the Apostle says

headnotes.la: …iti Filii Dei. Nihil aliud est ergo judicium, id est aeterna condemnatio, nisi non credere in Filium Dei, sicut nihil aliud est beatitudo et vita, nisi credere et cognoscere Filium Dei; sicut ipse ait
headnotes.en: …erefore, that is, eternal condemnation, is nothing else but not to believe in the Son of God, just as blessedness and life is nothing else but to believe and to know the Son of God; as he himself says

headnotes.la: *Hoc est autem judicium, quia lux venit in mundum.* Si lux non veniret in mundum, non esset de mundo judicium, sicut Dominus ait
headnotes.en: *And this is the judgment, that the light is come into the world.* If the light did not come into the world, there would be no judgment concerning the world, as the Lord says

headnotes.la: … cum discipulis suis, an cum credentibus in eum Judaeis, aut, quod verisimilius est, cum utrisque. *Et baptizavit.* Ubi quaeritur, si Christus ipse baptizavit, quomodo evangelista in sequentibus dicit
headnotes.en: …ether with his disciples, or with the Jews believing in him, or, which is more likely, with both. *And baptized.* Where it is asked, if Christ himself baptized, how the evangelist says in what follows

headnotes.la: …anitatis Christi per sacramentum baptismatis Joannis auctam fuisse. Quod maxime ex descensione Spiritus sancti in specie columbae super ipsum baptizatum argumentantur. Nec mirum, cum evangelista dicat
headnotes.en: …he sacrament of the baptism of John. This they argue chiefly from the descent of the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove upon him when he had been baptized. Nor is it a wonder, since the evangelist says

headnotes.la: …baptizare praesumentes, *et dixerunt ei: Rabbi, qui erat tecum trans Jordanem,* qui videbatur discipulus tuus tempore, quo a te baptizatus est trans Jordanem, *cui tu testimonium perhibuisti,* dicendo
headnotes.en: … *and said to him: Rabbi, he that was with thee beyond the Jordan,* who seemed to be thy disciple at the time when he was baptized by thee beyond the Jordan, *to whom thou gavest testimony,* by saying

headnotes.la: …m sciatis, quid ille sit, et quid ego sum, audite meum responsum: *Non potest homo accipere quicquam.* Homo sum et non Deus, ille vero et Deus est et homo. Ipse est, de quo testimonium perhibui dicens
headnotes.en: … am not. But that you may know what he is, and what I am, hear my answer: *A man cannot receive anything.* I am a man and not God, but he is both God and man. He it is of whom I bore testimony, saying

headnotes.la: …ipsius, cujus praecursor erat. Duo considerantur in homine: datum videlicet et donum. Datum refertur ad naturam, donum refertur ad gratiam. Et quamvis nullum horum sit nisi ex Deo, sicut ait Apostolus
headnotes.en: …was. Two things are considered in man: namely the given and the gift. The given is referred to nature, the gift is referred to grace. And although none of these is except from God, as the Apostle says

headnotes.la: …, ut inseparabilia fieri videantur. Nulla quippe natura est rationalis, quae omnino dono gratiae careat. *Nisi fuerit datum de caelo.* De quo caelo? De Patre videlicet. Audi Jacobum apostolum dicentem
headnotes.en: …ecome inseparable. For there is no rational nature which is wholly without the gift of grace. *Unless it be given from heaven.* From what heaven? From the Father, namely. Hear James the apostle saying

headnotes.la: … quod mihi testimonium adhibetis. *Quod dixerim: Ego non sum Christus, sed quia missus sum ante illum.* Audistis ex me haec verba, quando de eo loquebar ultra Jordanem; audistis utique, quando dicitis
headnotes.en: …ng testimony for me. *That I said: I am not the Christ, but that I am sent before him.* You heard these words from me when I was speaking of him beyond the Jordan; you heard them surely, since you say

headnotes.la: …nsam, sponsus est.* Videns praecursor cogitationes suorum discipulorum, qui talia de Christo ejusque baptismate proferebant, et audiebant sui magistri responsum de se ipso et de suo baptismate, dicens
headnotes.en: …The forerunner, seeing the thoughts of his disciples, who were putting forth such things about Christ and his baptism, and were hearing their master's answer concerning himself and his baptism, saying

headnotes.la: …l superat, quia omnia est. *Qui est de terra, terra est, et de terra loquitur.* De se ipso hoc ait, ac si diceret: Ego, qui de terra sum, hoc est de terrenis parentibus, natus ex illo, cui dictum est,
headnotes.en: …and speaketh of the earth.* [var: Vulg. *de terra est*, "is of the earth"] Of himself he says this, as if he said: I, who am of the earth, that is, of earthly parents, born of him to whom it was said,

headnotes.la: … in se ostendit. *Qui de caelo venit, super omnes est.* Eadem verba sunt, praeter quod prius *desursum venit,* nunc autem *de caelo venit.* Et quae est ista repetitio, et quid vult? An forte aliud est
headnotes.en: …at cometh from heaven is above all.* The words are the same, except that before it was *cometh from above,* but now *cometh from heaven.* And what is this repetition, and what does it mean? Or perhaps

headnotes.la: , aliud
headnotes.en: is one thing,

headnotes.la: ? Christus desursum venit, Christus de caelo venit, ideoque super omnes est, et super omnia. Potest itaque talis distantia inter
headnotes.en: another? Christ cometh from above, Christ cometh from heaven, and therefore is above all men, and above all things. Such a distinction, therefore, can be understood between

headnotes.la: et
headnotes.en: and

headnotes.la: intelligi, ut in eo, quod dixit
headnotes.en: , that in what he said,

headnotes.la: …ne ante peccatum? Carere peccato, quia humana natura, priusquam peccaret, omnino peccato carebat. Quid accepit ab homine post peccatum? Mori pro peccato, absque ullo reatu peccati. Quod ergo prius ait
headnotes.en: …sin? To be without sin, because human nature, before it sinned, was wholly without sin. What did he receive from man after sin? To die for sin, without any guilt of sin. What he said first, therefore,

headnotes.la: … ante peccatum processit. Quod autem in sequentibus dixit, *qui de caelo venit, super omnes est,* ibi intelligimus Patrem caeli nomine significatum, a quo missus est Christus in mundum, sicut ipse ait
headnotes.en: … But what he said in what follows, *he that cometh from heaven is above all,* there we understand the Father signified by the name of heaven, by whom Christ was sent into the world, as he himself says

headnotes.la: *Et quod vidit et audivit, hoc testatur.* Quid est, quod Filius Dei vidit? Non aliud, nisi cognovit, se in Patre, et aequalitatem ipsius esse. *Et audivit.* Quid audivit? Audivit a Patre
headnotes.en: …d, that he testifieth.* What is it that the Son of God saw? Nothing other than that he knew himself to be in the Father, and to be his equality. *And heard.* What did he hear? He heard from the Father

headnotes.la: …ivinitatem in suo Patre, et audivit a suo Patre, quod ipse eum genuerit aequalem sibi. *Hoc testatur.* Quid testatur? Quod Filius Dei sit. Et ubi testatur? Redige ad superiora, ubi ipse de se ipso ait
headnotes.en: …at he had begotten him equal to himself. *That he testifieth.* What does he testify? That he is the Son of God. And where does he testify it? Go back to what is above, where he himself says of himself

headnotes.la: …t tota sapientia, et in eo plenitudo donorum Dei. Propterea sequitur: *Non enim ex mensura dat Deus spiritum.* Ac si dixisset: Ex mensura dat Deus spiritum suum singulis hominibus, sicut ait Apostolus
headnotes.en: … him is the fullness of the gifts of God. Therefore there follows: *For God giveth not the spirit by measure.* As if he had said: God gives his spirit by measure to individual men, as the Apostle says

headnotes.la: , ceteraque spiritualium denorum divisio. Quibus verbis ostenditur, ex mensura dari Spiritum sanctum membris Ecclesiae. Quod consequenter ait Apostolus, dicens
headnotes.en: , and the rest of the division of spiritual gifts. By which words it is shown that the Holy Spirit is given by measure to the members of the Church. Which the Apostle says consequently, saying

headnotes.la: … *Pater diligit Filium,* ideo dedit ei totum suum spiritum, et omnia dedit in manu ejus. Quae omnia? An forte omnia, quae in ipso facta sunt? In principio enim fecit Deus caelum et terram; et psalmus,
headnotes.en: …n,* therefore he gave him his whole spirit, and gave all things into his hand. What all things? Perhaps all things that were made in him? For in the beginning God made heaven and earth; and the psalm,

headnotes.la: *Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam aeternam.* Quare? Quia ipse Filius vita aeterna est, sicut ipse ait
headnotes.en: *He that believeth in the Son hath life everlasting.* Why? Because the Son himself is life everlasting, as he himself says

headnotes.la: …dicit: ira Dei veniet super eum, sed ait: *manet super eum.* Quae est illa *ira Dei?* Nihil aliud, nisi maledictio illa, qua Deus maledixit primi hominis peccato, mandatum suum transgredientis, dicens
headnotes.en: …God will come upon him, but he says: *abideth upon him.* What is that *wrath of God?* Nothing else but that curse by which God cursed the sin of the first man, who transgressed his commandment, saying

headnotes.la: . Illius irae effectus est mors, et corruptio, et omnino veritatis ignorantia, quae omnia manent super eum. De illa ira ait Apostolus
headnotes.en: . The effect of that wrath is death, and corruption, and altogether ignorance of the truth, all which abide upon him. Of that wrath the Apostle says

headnotes.la: …n spiritualem ipsius litterae intellectum, qui per Galilaeam symbolice figuratur. Nec vacat quod ait: *Abiit iterum in Galilaeam.* De Galilaea enim venit in Judaeam, sicut in superioribus scriptum est
headnotes.en: …itual understanding of that letter, which is symbolically figured through Galilee. Nor is it idle that he says: *He went again into Galilee.* For from Galilee he came into Judaea, as was written above

headnotes.la: … Galilaea caelestis vitae ac divinae bonitatis figuram gerit, de qua Dominus nascens in carne venit in in Judaeam, hoc est, in sacramenta ipsius legis, quae primo Judaeis data est, sicut ait Apostolus
headnotes.en: …y life and of divine goodness, from which the Lord, being born in the flesh, came into [d: into] Judaea, that is, into the sacraments of that law which was first given to the Jews, as the Apostle says

headnotes.la: . Quoniam vero noluit manere sub lege, neque eos, qui in eum credituri essent, reliquit legem, ne sub lege essent, sed sub spiritu. Et hoc est, quod Apostolus ait,
headnotes.en: . But since he would not remain under the law, nor those who were to believe in him, he left the law, that they might not be under the law, but under the spirit. And this is what the Apostle says,

headnotes.la: …qua, quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in aeternum.* Ac si diceret: Cuicumque credenti in me donum sancti Spiritus a Patre per me procedentis dedero, non sitiet in aeternum. Dicturus enim est cum Psalmista
headnotes.en: …* As if he said: To whomsoever, believing in me, I shall have given the gift of the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father through me, [he] shall not thirst for ever. For he will say with the Psalmist

headnotes.la: …r itaque est anima rationalis, cujus vir intelligitur animus, qui multipliciter nominatur; aliquando enim intellectus, aliquando mens, aliquando animus, saepe etiam spiritus. De hoc viro ait Apostolus
headnotes.en: …ional soul, whose husband is understood [as] the *animus*, which is named in many ways; for sometimes intellect, sometimes mind, sometimes *animus*, often also spirit. Of this husband the Apostle says

headnotes.la: … gratia autem data, ut lex impleretur. Quoniam igitur lex litterae nil humanae naturae contulerit ad salutem, neminem enim lex ad perfectum duxit, sed ad cumulum delictorum valuit, sicut ait Apostolus
headnotes.en: …ight be fulfilled. Since therefore the law of the letter conferred nothing on human nature for salvation, for the law led no one to the perfect, but availed for a heap of offences, as the Apostle says

headnotes.la: , idem
headnotes.en: , and again

headnotes.la: …uem nescitis, nos autem adoramus eundem Patrem quem scimus. Nemo enim potest adorare Patrem, nisi prius adoraverit Filium. Qui credit in Filium, ipse novit Filium, ac per hoc novit et Patrem. Ait enim
headnotes.en: …dore the same Father whom we know. For no one can adore the Father unless he has first adored the Son. He who believes in the Son, he knows the Son, and through this knows the Father also. For he says

headnotes.la: *Dicit ei mulier: Scio, quia Messias venit, qui dicitur Christus.* Quoniam praedixit Dominus
headnotes.en: *The woman saith to him: I know that the Messias cometh, who is called Christ.* Since the Lord had said before,

headnotes.la: … de Messia, hoc est de venturo Christo, quem adhuc praesentem non cognoverat, quasi de alio dixisse. Audierat enim ex prophetis Christum venturum. Ideo ait: *Scio quia Messias venit. Venit* dixit, non
headnotes.en: …me, whom she did not yet know as present, as though of another. For she had heard from the prophets that Christ was to come. Therefore she says: *I know that the Messias cometh. Cometh,* she said, not

headnotes.la: …ntur, quia carnales homines illis pascebantur. Hordeum quippe jumentorum est proprie alimentum, non hominum. Carnalis populus adhuc sub littera degens, et vetustatem primi hominis, de quo scriptum est
headnotes.en: …re fed on them. For barley is properly the food of beasts of burden, not of men. The carnal people, still living under the letter, and not forsaking the oldness of the first man, of whom it is written

headnotes.la: …porei sensus et corporalia, quid sunt? quid prosunt ad tantam multitudinem fidelium, qui in te credituri sunt, et spiritualia alimenta petituri, quae omnem litteram omnemque corporeum sensum superant?
headnotes.en: … bodily things, what are they? what do they profit so great a multitude of the faithful, who are to believe in thee, and are to seek spiritual foods, which surpass every letter and every bodily sense?

headnotes.la: …mihi videtur profunditas, ut vix investigari queat. Augustinus quippe in expositione sua in Joannem nil inde tractat, sed omnino praetermisit. Quamquam multis sufficere videatur, quod in Marco legitur
headnotes.en: …ure, so that it can scarcely be searched out. For Augustine in his exposition on John treats nothing of it, but passed it over altogether. Although to many it may seem sufficient, what is read in Mark

headnotes.la: …adem. Sed si alia, non XII, sed XXIIII cophini fuerunt, si eadem, suffecerat dicere: tulerunt fragmentorum duodecim cophinos. Videtur non vacare mysterio, quod veluti post fragmenta panis collecta ait
headnotes.en: …I baskets; if the same, it had been sufficient to say: they took up twelve baskets of fragments. It seems not to be void of mystery that, as it were after the fragments of bread were gathered, he says

headnotes.la: …que Testamento et secundum historiam facta sunt, et secundum litteram narrata; symbola vero, quae solummodo non facta, sed quasi facta sola doctrina dicuntur. Verbi gratia, in veteri lege scriptum est
headnotes.en: … done according to history, and narrated according to the letter; but symbols are those which, only not done, but as it were done, are said by doctrine alone. For example, in the old law it is written

headnotes.la: … nunquam secundum historiam legitur fuisse, teste Augustino; dictum est tamen et scriptum, ac veluti factum traditur, cum veritas divinae historiae factum fuisse non invenitur narrare. Item in Psalmis
headnotes.en: …ing to history, as Augustine witnesses; yet it was said and written, and is handed down as though done, though the truth of divine history is not found to narrate that it was done. Again in the Psalms

headnotes.la: …se narrantur, qui, veluti discipuli, cum Christo in altitudinem contemplationis, tanquam in quendam montem ascendunt, relictis carnalibus, sub littera et sensu in foeno rerum temporalium recumbentibus
headnotes.en: …like the disciples, ascend with Christ into the height of contemplation, as into a certain mountain, the carnal being left behind, lying down under the letter and sense in the grass of temporal things

headnotes.la: …infra altitudinem divinorum intellectuum residentem. Nam ex textu Evangelii datur intelligi, non in summitate montis, sed in quadam planitie, ubi foenum multum fuerat, Dominum turbam pavisse. Ubi ait,
headnotes.en: …ndings. For from the text of the Gospel it is given to understand that the Lord fed the crowd not on the summit of the mountain, but on a certain plain, where there had been much grass. Where he says,

headnotes.la: , inquit,
headnotes.en: , he says,

headnotes.la: . Ecce historiae prima fragmenta simplicibus sufficientia. Consequenter subjungit fragmenta spiritualia, dicens
headnotes.en: . Behold the first fragments of history, sufficient for the simple. Consequently he subjoins the spiritual fragments, saying

headnotes.la: …eteris autem sensibus percipi non potest. Legitur enim oculis, auribus auditur, olfactu vero seu gustu seu tactu remota est. Verbi gratia, ut eisdem utamur exemplis, legatur quod scriptum est in Exodo
headnotes.en: … the other senses. For it is read with the eyes, heard with the ears, but it is removed from smell or taste or touch. For example, to use the same examples, let that be read which is written in Exodus

headnotes.la: …ttera et spiritu confectum partim perit, partim aeternaliter manet. Perit quod videtur, quia sensibile est et temporale; manet quod non videtur, quia spirituale est et aeternale. Symboli exemplum fiat
headnotes.en: …es, partly remains eternally. That perishes which is seen, because it is sensible and temporal; that remains which is not seen, because it is spiritual and eternal. Let an example of a symbol be given
